threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—that's a rookie mistake around here.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and there was a guy practicing drum beats on his lap. Can't say I wasn't entertained!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy casually fixing his bike on the sidewalk while a street musician played Bossa Nova on the corner. That's Neukölln life.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can catch a bus driver singing karaoke over the intercom during a strike. Only here do the delays come with entertainment!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for the BART delays—while newcomers just check their apps, we already know to plan for an hour lost.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, a guy played Beethoven on a battery-powered keyboard inside the bus. Half the riders were jamming while the other half just rolled their eyes.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think locals live on tapas and paella. Meanwhile, we're all about that homemade esqueixada and some proper fuet from the market.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their pronounced excitement while ordering a cortado, still pronouncing it as 'cor-ta-do' instead of 'cor-tao.'

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' when it’s just the London Overground. Locals know it’s a vibe, not just a route.
Last night on the 196, a guy was loudly singing opera. No one joined in, but we all pretended it was normal. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy fixing his bike in front of a café, chatting with the barista over pastries. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night Kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery, where the walls are covered in ever-changing street art.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission if they can spot the difference between taco trucks on 24th and 26th without breaking a sweat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a guy in a full tuxedo jump on the 14, only to pull out a saxophone and start playing. Typical Mission magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars serve vermut on tap. Try finding one that does outside Gràcia; it’s like searching for needles in haystacks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the sheer number of ferreteries—who knew you’d need a hardware store for every neighborhood?
